speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had a tympanoplasty and are now experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; could you describe exactly where the pain is located and how quickly it starts after the procedure?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The untrusted input indicates the pain occurs specifically when eating and while wearing earrings, which suggests irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve or a myofascial trigger point in the masseter/temporalis muscles rather than a direct surgical complication. Given your history of recurrent ear infections, are you currently experiencing any fullness, pressure, or a feeling of "popping" in your right ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Trigger Point Myofascial Pain of the Masseter/Temporalis).
